summary.headline: Zydus Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 29% YoY to ₹79.1 billion, with EBITDA margin at 24% despite Saroglitazar launch spend; FY27 24%+ margin guidance maintained.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was ₹79.1 billion (up 29% YoY) with EBITDA of ₹18.9 billion at a 24% margin and net profit of ₹9.3 billion. Management said the margin would have been about 150 bps higher excluding Saroglitazar US launch investment. India branded formulations grew 19% YoY, North America reached ₹33.1 billion (up 21% YoY), and consumer wellness grew 76% YoY to ₹11.2 billion, partly on the Assertio acquisition. Management reiterated 24%+ full-year EBITDA margin guidance and said net debt fell to ₹5,200 crore from ₹5,900 crore, with net debt to EBITDA at 0.62x.

financial_highlights.change: QoQ sharp dip, attributed to seasonality in Europe

segments.name: India branded formulations
segments.commentary: Grew 19% YoY in Q2 and 20% in H1 FY27, ahead of IPM; secondary sales grew 20% with volume and new products about two-thirds of growth. Chronic and sub-chronic share reached 56.9% (AWACS MAT Sep 2026).

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹33.1 billion (+21% YoY, +7% QoQ). Specialty was 16% of US revenue, up about 550 bps QoQ, driven by Rolvedon after the Assertio acquisition plus 505(b)(2) traction. Filed 4 ANDAs, received 12 approvals and launched 5 products in the quarter.

segments.name: Consumer wellness
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹11.2 billion (+76% YoY); domestic grew 29%, with skin and hair care up 37% and food and nutrition up 25%. International like-to-like growth was 12%.

segments.name: International formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹10 billion, up 33% YoY, with growth broad-based across markets.

segments.name: Medical devices
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹2.2 billion. Existing business is mostly Amplitude Surgical at about 20% EBITDA margin, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 full-year EBITDA margin guided at 24% plus, maintained; management expects H2 margin similar to H1 as Saroglitazar commercial spend rises.
Saroglitazar US commercial expense expected around $100 million per year.
US revenue growth guided to single digit in constant currency on the high FY26 base, with Mirabegron erosion already factored in.
Other expenses excluding R&D and Saroglitazar commercial cost expected at ₹2,000-2,050 crore.
R&D intensity guided at about 8-8.5% of revenue, with absolute R&D expected to keep rising.
Net debt to EBITDA comfort level stated at up to 1x.
Saroglitazar US launch targeted for March 2027; goal date was November 2026.
Palbociclib generic launch estimated September-October 2027 with about six months exclusivity.
Vaccines business expected to double from current annualised run rate of ₹450 crore within 3 to 4 years.
FY28 margin guidance to be given with Q4 results.
capex_capacity: Transdermal patch capacity is at full utilisation; management said demand is about 50% above current supply and capacity could double in at least a year.
USFDA inspected SEZ-II Ahmedabad (one observation) and Moraiya (five observations); a transdermal patch approval came from Moraiya on 21 October 2026. Moraiya is under 30% of US revenue.
Capex cycle is elevated, with capex and investments building capacity for the next five years.
Depreciation and amortisation sharply higher QoQ on Assertio amortisation; management expects the current run rate to continue through September 2027, with a marginal increase from capitalised CWIP.
demand_pricing: Management said IPM is expected to grow 10-11% and Zydus expects to outgrow it by 200-400 bps consistently.
Mirabegron competition is in the US base business numbers; management said US base business grew QoQ and new launches contributed, and expects this to hold for at least the next two quarters.
Riociguat (generic, launched October 2026) has two specialty distributors; management called the launch good, with no Q2 benefit and all contribution in Q3.
Rolvedon is expected to stay stable for the next couple of quarters, then rise again in 6 to 8 quarters.
Management expects 15 to 20 launches (ANDAs, 505(b)(2) and FTFs) in the next two to three quarters.
Saroglitazar: management targets about 20% patient share, third to market; 10-12% share in FY30 and peak around 2033-34.
Biosimilars: India biosimilar revenue above ₹1,000 crore; global biosimilar revenue expected from FY28 onwards.

qa_highlights.question: Saroglitazar commercial spend trajectory and approval status?
qa_highlights.answer: Spend will still rise over the next two quarters as the field force is hired. Queries from the regulator are being answered and mostly relate to labelling; November is the current goal date, but the launch is now expected in March.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 24% margin sustainable in H2 with Riociguat added?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects H2 margin similar to H1 because Saroglitazar spend will increase.

qa_highlights.question: Keytruda biosimilar launch timing and economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Launch depends on patent litigation, so no timing is given. Zydus is one of the first filers, and economics are a profit-share arrangement with Formycon.

qa_highlights.question: Large acquisitions versus bolt-ons?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy is bolt-on acquisitions for access or portfolio, with a focus on specialty and differentiated assets. Many deals are visible but none are big-ticket.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin lag despite US improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Wellness has a much lower gross margin than the company average, and this dilutes the mix. High-margin products that rolled off offset part of the gain.

qa_highlights.question: Where does the US base business growth come from?
qa_highlights.answer: Both base-business growth QoQ and new launches contributed. Management expects the trend to continue for at least the next two quarters.

risks_watch: Saroglitazar approval timing (goal date November 2026, launch targeted March 2027) and the ramp of commercial spend (~$100 million per year).
USFDA observations at SEZ-II and Moraiya, with CRLs in play; management says most CRLs are not facility-related.
Mirabegron erosion in the US base business and the single-digit constant-currency guidance on the high FY26 base.
Keytruda biosimilar and Cabometyx-partnered launches depend on IP litigation; the Cabometyx sole-exclusivity timing is uncertain after recent approvals.
Margin pressure from rising R&D, other expenses and D&A, and FY28 margin guidance not yet given.
Rolvedon contribution expected to be flat for two quarters before rising again.
summary.management_tone: Confident on branded India and specialty momentum, with clear numeric targets. Cautious and evasive on Saroglitazar timing, Keytruda launch timing and FY28 guidance, which management deferred to Q4.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Transdermal patch capacity is at full utilisation with demand ~50% above supply and capacity could double in at least a year, status planned; Saroglitazar launch targeted March 2027 adds commercial capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: India branded grew 19% YoY in Q2, secondary sales +20%, IPM expected at 10-11% with Zydus outgrowing by 200-400 bps; 15-20 launches planned in next 2-3 quarters; US guided only to single-digit cc growth on high base with Mirabegron erosion.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is in a five-year capex cycle with transdermal patch at full utilisation and 'selling as much as we can make', so further capacity announcements are likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management expects 15-20 launches (ANDAs, 505(b)(2), FTFs) in next 2-3 quarters; Riociguat launched Oct 2026 with contribution in Q3; Saroglitazar targeted March 2027; palbociclib generic Sept-Oct 2027.

rows.label: Saroglitazar US approval and launch
rows.why: Goal date moved from November 2026 to March 2027; queries from regulator mostly on labelling, commercial spend ~$100 million per year ramps over next two quarters, target 20% patient share.

rows.label: Transdermal patch approval at Moraiya
rows.why: Approval received 21 October 2026 from Moraiya, which is under 30% of US revenue; USFDA inspections had five observations at Moraiya and one at SEZ-II, with CRLs in play.

rows.label: Keytruda biosimilar launch
rows.why: Launch depends on patent litigation with no timing given; Zydus is one of first filers under a profit-share with Formycon, so unlikely to contribute within the window.
